summary: Headless audits are clean on both phone and desktop. Axe reported no violations, Lighthouse accessibility and best practices scored 100, nothing overflowed horizontally, and there were no console errors. The full primary flow passed on both viewports: Home → Book a consultation → contact errors → focused teal border → filled → success. The secondary flows also passed: services hash scroll below the sticky header, training filter, about and not-found. Every screen and state in the spec was captured. Most source files were over the review budget, so this review relies on the audit results and the visible files. The one concrete defect is a class in the markup with no CSS rule, which the spec explicitly forbids. The other note is a minor consistency gap in client-side metadata.

findings.issue: phase-2 fix U1: Message textarea (pristine): The Message field shows a red error border before the user has typed in it or submitted. This reads as an error and adds friction for a skeptical visitor. Expected after the fix: In the contact form component, apply the invalid border class and aria-invalid only when the field is touched (after blur) or after a submit attempt. Pristine fields keep the default outline border.

phase-2 fix U2: Contact page hero/intro section (desktop): On desktop the h1 'Book a consultation' starts about 4px below the header bottom (y=72 to 75), so it looks clipped and cramped. Phone has generous top space. Expected after the fix: Give the contact page container padding-top: 64px at the desktop breakpoint (≥1024px), matching the phone rhythm. Keep 48px between the intro block and the form card top, then align the form card's top with the h1's top.

phase-2 fix U3: Left intro column (desktop): Below the email line the left column is a ~550px empty void beside the long form, which makes the layout feel unbalanced. Expected after the fix: Make the intro column position: sticky with top: calc(var(--header-h) + 48px) and align-self: start. It then stays beside the form while the user scrolls. Copy is unchanged.

phase-2 fix U4: 'What can we help with?' select: The select's text inset is ~20px on phone versus 15px on the inputs, and ~19px versus 15px on desktop. The text column is visibly misaligned in the form stack. Expected after the fix: In the contact form CSS, set the select to padding: 0 40px 0 16px with the same height, border and font-size as the text inputs. Use appearance: none with a 16px chevron background at right 16px so the text aligns with the input text.

findings.screen: services training section below sticky header
findings.issue: phase-2 fix U5: Section separators and vertical padding (phone): On phone there is ~75px of space above the divider and ~75px below it before the 'TRAINING' eyebrow. The 'Typical engagement' line floats away from its own cards. Expected after the fix: On the services page at <768px, set section padding-block to 48px (was ~72px+). Give the 'Typical engagement' line margin-top: 16px under the card list.
The style audit shows the class `home-page` is used in the markup but matches no CSS rule. DESIGN.md requires that every class used in the markup has a CSS rule, so this is a dead hook.
findings.fix: Either remove `className="home-page"` from the Home page wrapper, or add a real rule for it in src/styles/global.css. If the wrapper needs no styling, removing the class is the cleaner option.

findings.issue: On client-side route changes, only `document.title` is updated. The meta description, og tags and canonical link stay as they were for the first page loaded. Prerendered files are correct for crawlers and shared links. However, a hydrated session that navigates from Home to /services keeps Home's description and canonical in the DOM. This is inconsistent with the per-page metadata table.
findings.fix: Extend the hook to also update `meta[name=description]`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url` and `link[rel=canonical]` from `getPageMeta(pathname)`. Do this inside the same effect, so first-load markup is unchanged and still matches the prerendered output.

findings.issue: The form fields are too close to the top of the card and lack sufficient padding above and below the form group, making it feel cramped and unpolished.
findings.fix: Add padding above and below the form card to create breathing room and improve visual hierarchy.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badges are too small and lack visual weight relative to the field labels, making them hard to notice.
findings.fix: Increase the size and contrast of the 'Required' badges to make them more prominent and accessible.

findings.issue: The form is positioned too far to the right, leaving large empty space on the left, which feels unbalanced and underutilized.
findings.fix: Center the form or adjust the layout to better utilize the available space on desktop.

findings.issue: The form fields have no placeholder text or hint, which reduces usability for new users.
findings.fix: Add placeholder text to each field to guide users on what to enter.

findings.issue: The 'Message' field is missing a 'Required' badge, even though it's required.
findings.fix: Add a 'Required' badge to the 'Message' field to maintain consistency.

findings.issue: The form card has a subtle border and shadow, but the contrast with the background is low, making it feel flat.
findings.fix: Increase the contrast of the card border or add a more pronounced shadow to make it stand out.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'contact form empty' (target 8+, minimum 7): The contact form is clean and functional with good visual hierarchy and consistent spacing, but lacks polish in typography, spacing, and form controls that would elevate it to a polished commercial product. The desktop layout is underutilized and the form fields are visually underwhelming.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badge is positioned to the right of the label, which can be confusing on small screens where the label is short. It should be inline with the field or directly below for better clarity.
findings.fix: Reposition the 'Required' badge to be inline with the label or directly below it, ensuring it’s visually connected to the field it describes.

findings.issue: The error message for 'Name' is positioned directly under the input field, which is correct, but the red border is slightly thicker than the other fields, creating visual inconsistency.
findings.fix: Standardize the border thickness across all input fields, including error states, to maintain visual uniformity.

findings.issue: The form card is not fully aligned to the left edge of the viewport; there is a small margin on the left, which is acceptable, but could be more intentional for a polished look.
findings.fix: Adjust the left margin to be more intentional and consistent with the overall spacing system, perhaps aligning the card to the left edge with a consistent left padding.

findings.issue: The 'Company' input field has a thick, teal border indicating focus, which is inconsistent with the thin, grey borders on other fields. This creates visual hierarchy but feels unbalanced and may confuse users.
findings.fix: Apply a consistent focus state across all fields (e.g., subtle outline or shadow) to maintain visual harmony.

findings.issue: The 'Message' field is partially visible, cut off at the bottom of the screen. This is a critical usability issue as users cannot complete the form.
findings.fix: Ensure the entire form is visible on phone view by adjusting padding or container height.

findings.issue: The form is positioned too far right, leaving large empty space on the left. This feels unbalanced and underutilizes the desktop real estate.
findings.fix: Center or left-align the form with appropriate padding to fill the space without appearing cramped or sparse.

findings.issue: The 'Required' labels are small and placed in a small pill, which may be overlooked by users, especially on smaller screens.
findings.fix: Increase the size of the 'Required' indicator or use a more prominent visual cue (e.g., red asterisk) to ensure visibility.

findings.issue: The 'What can we help with?' dropdown has no placeholder text or hint, making it unclear what options are available.
findings.fix: Add a placeholder or tooltip to guide users on selecting a topic.

findings.issue: The 'Prefer email?' link is styled as a hyperlink but lacks visual distinction from regular text, making it less noticeable.
findings.fix: Use a different color or icon to visually distinguish the email link from the surrounding text.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'contact field focused teal border' (target 8+, minimum 7): The contact form is clean and functional, with clear visual hierarchy and consistent spacing. It meets basic usability standards for a professional service. However, it lacks polish in form field styling, error states, and desktop layout refinement that would elevate it to 'polished' status.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The 'Required' labels are placed to the right of the field labels, which is unconventional and may confuse users. Labels should typically be above or to the left of inputs.
findings.fix: Reposition 'Required' indicators to be inline with the field labels or above them, maintaining consistent alignment with the form structure.

findings.issue: The 'Message' textarea is partially cut off at the bottom on the phone view, suggesting insufficient height or clipping.
findings.fix: Ensure the textarea has sufficient height to display all content without clipping, or adjust padding/margin to prevent overflow.

findings.issue: The dropdown for 'What can we help with?' is not visually distinct from the other fields, lacking a clear indicator of its interactive nature.
findings.fix: Add a subtle visual cue (e.g., border, background color, or icon) to indicate the dropdown is interactive and can be expanded.

findings.issue: The form is slightly misaligned with the left margin of the page, creating an inconsistent visual rhythm.
findings.fix: Adjust the form's left margin to align with the page's main content block, ensuring consistent spacing and alignment with the header and other elements.

findings.issue: The 'Required' labels are too small and positioned too close to the input fields, reducing readability and accessibility.
findings.fix: Increase the size of the 'Required' labels and increase vertical spacing between them and the input fields.

findings.issue: The form container has inconsistent padding on the left and right, causing misalignment with the overall layout.
findings.fix: Apply consistent horizontal padding to the form container to align it with the page's grid.

findings.issue: The form container is slightly too narrow, causing the text fields to appear cramped and reducing usability.
findings.fix: Increase the width of the form container to allow for better spacing and improved readability.

findings.issue: The 'Menu' button is positioned too far right, causing the header to appear unbalanced on small screens.
findings.fix: Center the header elements or adjust the menu button's padding to create a more balanced layout.

findings.issue: The 'Book a consultation' CTA button is not visible in the menu on phone, which may break the primary action accessibility.
findings.fix: Ensure the CTA button is visible and accessible within the mobile menu, perhaps by placing it at the bottom or using a full-width button.

findings.issue: The 'Book a consultation' button is slightly too wide, causing a visual imbalance with the nav links.
findings.fix: Adjust the button width to better align with the nav links or reduce padding to create a more cohesive look.

findings.issue: Hero h1 to lede spacing (desktop): On desktop the lede starts ~24px under a 56px serif h1, which is tighter than the phone version. The hero reads crowded next to the airy illustration.
findings.fix: On the home hero at ≥1024px, set the h1 margin-bottom to 24px. Set the lede margin-bottom to 40px before the button row and cap the lede at max-width: 56ch.
